memory_update.text: HMDPF/HPS.A should be tracked as the cleanest discovered dry-type transformer and power-quality exposure, but it is US OTC rather than primary US exchange listed.

POWL maps strongly to medium-voltage switchgear, E-Houses, bus duct, and engineered power-distribution systems; evidence of large data-center orders moves it from generic industrial to direct power-chain candidate.
PLPC is not in transformers but is a second-order transmission/distribution hardware chokepoint candidate; survival in later layers requires order/backlog evidence linked to utility grid buildout.

The node should be broadened from dry-type transformers only to a schedule-critical electrical balance-of-system cluster: transformers, switchgear, E-Houses, bus systems, enclosures, PDUs, connectors, and T&D line hardware.

Need a focused later pass on distributors and channel bottlenecks such as WESCO-like electrical distribution, because transformer/switchgear shortages can be expressed through procurement and availability rather than manufacturing alone.

node: Dry-type transformers, power-quality products, electrical magnetics, and power-distribution equipment
summary: Layer 1B expansion for the power-distribution chokepoint suggests that the most relevant underfollowed lane is not generation owners but manufacturers and component suppliers tied to medium-voltage distribution, dry-type transformers, switchgear, bus systems, power enclosures, and transmission/distribution hardware. The list intentionally includes one reference/context name plus three less-obvious US-traded or US-listed candidates. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation.
